# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Threshold point: "[STANDARD]" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's package marks most clauses "[STANDARD]". It says these have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that "the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." **I have not relied on this.**

- It is the counterparty's own characterisation, in its own draft.
- Nothing in our playbook records any such agreement.
- Several "[STANDARD]" items are exactly the positions our playbook rejects.
- The playbook also treats several matters as OPEN, including Tax/IP.

I have reviewed every clause on its merits. I recommend we tell Seller's counsel in writing that we do not accept the pre-categorisation or the claimed agreement. That stops it being cited later as an estoppel or course-of-dealing argument.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000).
- **Recommendation: REJECT. Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% fallback needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation: REJECT. Counter at 5k / 50k tipping.** The Seller's thresholds are 5x ours, and the deductible structure permanently shields the first AUD 250,000.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months. Also, "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims. Separate, longer periods for Fundamental/Title and others.
- **Recommendation: REJECT. Counter at 24 months, and delete the "applies to all Claims" sentence.** The 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost's written approval (none given). The default-application sentence is a hidden override (see SPA-N-014).

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties fall under the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with:
  - a 100% cap;
  - a period of at least six years;
  - no general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay for. Capping them at 20% for 18 months is not an administrative point.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No express carve-out. Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "to all Claims of any nature." On its face this sweeps in fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all of the following, to the maximum extent enforceable:
  - caps;
  - baskets;
  - time limits;
  - exclusive remedy;
  - non-reliance.
- **Recommendation: REJECT. Insert an express, overriding carve-out.** This is non-negotiable under the playbook. No one may waive it, and the "[STANDARD]" label does not change that.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7 / DL 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (as at 22 Sep 2026), the Accounts, the statutory registers and all public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only, against identified warranties.
- **Recommendation: REJECT DL 1.1 and 1.2.** Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure would let the Seller defeat claims with anything buried anywhere. Specific disclosures (DL 2–10) can stand, subject to our comments below. Also note that DL 1.4's non-admission language must not dilute the specific disclosures.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer *or its advisers*, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** The blanket exclusion deleted. Any qualifier should rest on named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: DELETE cl 8.3.** Combined with constructive "discoverable" knowledge, it would gut the warranties and even the specific indemnities. We have flagged Bluefen, Riverlark and Ironquay ourselves, so this clause would hand the Seller a defence on exactly those.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of a written consent.
- **Facts:** DL 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m).
- **Buyer wants:** Two things before Completion, as a condition precedent:
  - an effective consent; and
  - evidence that its cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** A consent letter that is conditional and whose conditions are unmet does not protect a 30% customer. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a consent this material.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Seller:** A release "to be provided following Completion." About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, and DL 3 confirms it is not repaid and not discharged.
- **Buyer wants:** At Completion:
  - a current payout letter;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds; and
  - executed, effective security releases (including PPSR and any mortgage discharges).
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** A post-completion release leaves us owning a company with live change-control (cl 8.1) and security exposure. That alternative would need an irrevocable bank undertaking *and* Amelia Frost's approval, and neither exists.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005)
- **Seller:** The AUD 420,000 is "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses plus any triggered on-costs handled in one of two ways:
  - as a specific funds-flow line item (deducted from price or paid directly), or
  - expressly Seller-funded, backed by an indemnity.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the silent exclusion.** These obligations crystallise in the Company on Completion. If they are not itemised, the Buyer effectively bears them. On-costs need quantifying.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate."
- **Facts:** DL 4 states DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, and that this is *not* independent verification. It also notes no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering:
  - IP ownership, title and infringement losses from the Ironquay arrangement;
  - the cost of obtaining a confirmatory assignment; and
  - preserving the SOW3 cure (cleared payment triggering transfer under DD-004 cl 7.3).
- **Recommendation: REJECT "adequate"; broaden the indemnity.** The risk is non-transfer of the Project Materials, not just a fee. Neither side should treat the AUD 180,000 figure as established. Seek verification, for example an Ironquay statement or bank evidence.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006; cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material."
- **Facts (DL 6):** About 1,240 records may have been exposed. Access, scope and any notification duty are not established.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - log preservation;
  - a completed investigation;
  - regular updates to the Buyer before Completion;
  - an assessment of notification obligations under the Privacy Act (NDB scheme) and any other applicable regime; and
  - appropriate warranty/indemnity protection.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the materiality characterisation; add covenants.** We should not accept "not material" before the facts are known. Equally, we should *not* assert a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any numeric demand, because the record does not support those either.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Seller:** AUD 330,000 (3 × 110k) of "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Facts:** DL 8 itself does not state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of timing, scope, terminability and accrual status before deciding treatment.
- **Recommendation: DO NOT ACCEPT the Seller's characterisation yet; investigate.** The disclosure does not support "ordinary course." Per the playbook, we also should not automatically treat these as Debt or demand a price deduction. Treatment follows the assessment.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Two provisions merge the categories:
  - "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13).
  - Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply "to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, specific-indemnity/payment and covenant claims each kept in separate, express regimes. Those regimes should prevail over the general limitations.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the default-application language.** It operates as a hidden override that collapses every category into the general 20% / 18-month package. Add an express hierarchy clause instead.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title to 100% of the shares is "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012.
- **Facts:** DL 10 concedes the register only identifies the Seller's source, and does not state that the Buyer has verified it.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of:
  - title;
  - ownership;
  - absence of encumbrances; and
  - authority.

  Suitable evidence includes an ASIC company extract, a PPSR search against the Seller and the shares, constitution and share-issue documentation, Seller board/authority resolutions, and an unencumbered-title warranty under the Fundamental regime.
- **Recommendation: REJECT reliance on DD-012 alone.** It is an internal, Seller-supplied record, not independent proof. This is also why the Fundamental regime (SPA-N-004) matters.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** These terms remain OPEN. Neither side has agreed them, and we assume neither a resolution nor unlimited liability.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the "settled" characterisation; keep the terms open.** Nothing in our playbook records agreement. Folding Tax/IP into the 20% / 18-month regime would also pre-empt negotiation of separate treatment, which is often appropriate given how long tax exposures can last.

---

## Summary and next steps

| # | Issue | Position |
|---|---|---|
| 001 | Cap | Reject: 25% / AUD 6m |
| 002 | Thresholds | Reject: 5k / 50k tipping |
| 003 | Time limit | Reject: 24 months; delete "all Claims" sentence |
| 004 | Fundamental/Title | Reject: 100% / 6+ yrs / outside general limits |
| 005 | Fraud | Reject: express overriding carve-out (non-waivable) |
| 006 | Disclosure | Reject DL 1.1–1.2: specific disclosure only |
| 007 | Buyer knowledge | Delete cl 8.3 |
| 008 | Bluefen | Reject: effective consent + conditions satisfied, as a CP |
| 009 | Riverlark | Reject: payout, direct repayment, releases at Completion |
| 010 | Bonuses | Reject: line item or Seller-funded, incl. on-costs |
| 011 | Ironquay | Broaden indemnity; keep SOW3 cure; verify AUD 180k |
| 012 | DD-006 incident | Covenants; no materiality concession; no overstated claims |
| 013 | Sandbar | Investigate; no auto Debt or deduction |
| 014 | Categories | Reject override; add hierarchy clause |
| 015 | Title | Require independent evidence beyond DD-012 |
| 016 | Tax/IP | Remains OPEN |

**Escalation points for Amelia Frost:**
- No fallback (20% cap, 18 months, post-completion Riverlark release) has been authorised. The mark-up should therefore go out at starting positions.
- If the deal team wants any fallback in play, it needs her prior written authority referencing this draft.
- The fraud carve-out cannot be traded by anyone.

**Covering note to Seller's counsel:** It should state that we do not accept the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] pre-categorisation or the asserted agreement on the disclosure and limitation package, and that all clauses remain subject to our mark-up.

  - an assessment of notification obligations under the Privacy Act (NDB scheme) and any other applicable regime; and
  - appropriate warranty/indemnity protection.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the materiality characterisation; add covenants.** We should not accept "not material" before the facts are known. Equally, we should *not* assert a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any numeric demand, because the record does not support those either.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Seller:** AUD 330,000 (3 × 110k) of "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Facts:** DL 8 itself does not state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of timing, scope, terminability and accrual status before deciding treatment.
- **Recommendation: DO NOT ACCEPT the Seller's characterisation yet; investigate.** The disclosure does not support "ordinary course." Per the playbook, we also should not automatically treat these as Debt or demand a price deduction. Treatment follows the assessment.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Two provisions merge the categories:
  - "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13).
  - Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply "to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, specific-indemnity/payment and covenant claims each kept in separate, express regimes. Those regimes should prevail over the general limitations.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the default-application language.** It operates as a hidden override that collapses every category into the general 20% / 18-month package. Add an express hierarchy clause instead.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title to 100% of the shares is "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012.
- **Facts:** DL 10 concedes the register only identifies the Seller's source, and does not state that the Buyer has verified it.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of:
  - title;
  - ownership;
  - absence of encumbrances; and
  - authority.

  Suitable evidence includes an ASIC company extract, a PPSR search against the Seller and the shares, constitution and share-issue documentation, Seller board/authority resolutions, and an unencumbered-title warranty under the Fundamental regime.
- **Recommendation: REJECT reliance on DD-012 alone.** It is an internal, Seller-supplied record, not independent proof. This is also why the Fundamental regime (SPA-N-004) matters.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** These terms remain OPEN. Neither side has agreed them, and we assume neither a resolution nor unlimited liability.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the "settled" characterisation; keep the terms open.** Nothing in our playbook records agreement. Folding Tax/IP into the 20% / 18-month regime would also pre-empt negotiation of separate treatment, which is often appropriate given how long tax exposures can last.
